bib.title: Do Prompt-Based Models Really Understand the Meaning of Their Prompts?
bib.venue: NAACL 2022 (Proceedings of the 2022 Conference of the North American Chapter of the ACL: HLT, pages 2300-2344)

read.skipped: Per-template accuracy tables and plot axis residue in Appendices G-J read only in outline (numbers are in figures/tables not needed for claims).

question: Do prompt-based models use prompt templates as semantically meaningful task instructions the way humans do?
hypothesis: Null/implicit: the commonly assumed hypothesis is that models benefit from meaningful instructions; the authors test it and expect instructive templates to beat irrelevant/misleading ones if models understand them.
contributions: Over 30 manually written NLI templates in 5 categories and 13 LM target-word sets (over 390 prompts) evaluated zero- and few-shot
Show irrelevant and misleading templates yield about the same few-shot learning speed as instructive ones, up to GPT-3 175B and instruction-tuned T0
Show the choice of LM target words matters much more than template meaning

method.summary: Manually written discrete prompt templates for NLI (RTE) in five categories (instructive, misleading-moderate, misleading-extreme, irrelevant, null) are used with rank classification of target words. Models are fine-tuned on k={4..256} examples (ALBERT, T5 LM-Adapted, T0) or primed (GPT-3 davinci, 16 shots), and accuracy is compared across template categories and target-word categories with significance tests.
method.task: Natural language inference (RTE, binary) with prompt-based few-shot and zero-shot learning

datasets.name: RTE (SuperGLUE collection, binary)
datasets.size: n = 2490 training examples for full set; k-shot subsets 4-256
datasets.split: validation accuracy reported; few-shot training examples are consecutive indices from a seed-specific start (seed 1: 550-553 for 4-shot)

datasets.name: ANLI R1, HANS, WSC
datasets.source: Nie et al. 2020; McCoy et al. 2019; Levesque et al. 2012

other.note: chosen as baseline after preliminary tests of BERT, DistilBERT, RoBERTa, ALBERT, T5

models.name: T0 / T0++
models.init_from: Sanh et al. 2021; trained on over 60 datasets, hundreds of prompts, NLI held out

models.name: GPT-3 davinci
models.context: 2049 tokens (API limit), so max 16 priming shots

other.primed not fine-tuned: fine-tuning API limited to 10 runs/month, 5 epochs, models up to 6.7B

training.objective: prompt-based fine-tuning; rank classification of single-token target words
training.optimizer: AdamW (PyTorch Adafactor gave substantially worse T5 results)
training.epochs: 30 (20 for 11B models); checkpoint with highest validation accuracy selected
training.hardware: ALBERT: 1x RTX3090; T5 770M: 1x A6000; 3B: layers split over 4x RTX3090; 11B: 8x V100 32GB
training.compute: approx 192 GPU hours (ALBERT), 48 (T5 770M), 2,304 (3B models T5 and T0), 1,728 (11B models T5, T0, T0++)
training.seeds: 4 random seeds (same set for all experiments); GPT-3 single run

other.EOS: EOS added for few-shot inputs (following Raffel), omitted at zero-shot to reproduce Sanh et al.
other.lr search: 3e-4, 1e-4, 5e-5, 1e-5 tried in preliminary runs, not exhaustive

inference.decoding: rank classification over single-token target words (no sampling, beam, top-k or top-p)
inference.samples: 4 seeds for fine-tuned models; GPT-3 one run, 16 priming shots, different priming examples per inference example
inference.prompting: {premise} template text {hypothesis} [prediction]; default targets yes/no; GPT-3 uses separator \n###\n between priming examples, no trailing space, leading-space target token

parameters.prompts: over 30 templates x 13 LM target sets, over 390 prompts

metrics.name: RTE validation accuracy
metrics.definition: rank classification: correct if gold target word probability exceeds the other class's

baselines: Schick and Schutze 2021b reported 69.8% on RTE at 32 shots
eval.protocol: 4 seeds; ANOVA and Kruskal-Wallis, then pairwise independent two-sample t-test and Wilcoxon rank-sum, alpha 0.05 with Bonferroni; both tests agree; no practical difference means very small effect sizes

availability.data: RTE, public; training example indices in GitHub repo

limits: Absence of significant difference does not entail no difference; argument rests on small effect sizes (footnote 3)
Only NLI (RTE) in the main text; ANLI, HANS, WSC are preliminary appendices
Lack of competence at zero shots: non-instruction-tuned models near random, so null results there are ambiguous
Accuracy cannot directly measure understanding; lack of compliance and spurious-feature interactions not ruled out
GPT-3 only primed at 16 shots, single run, different priming examples per inference example, not comparable to the fine-tuned models' fixed shots
11B models limited to 0 and 16 shots; Adafactor replaced with AdamW
Prompts written by the authors; GPT-3 zero-shot on RTE reproduced only with Brown et al.'s exact prompt, other prompts at random
